means: A pluggable provider path that serves harness turns through Claude, behind the existing provider seam, beside OpenRouter.
A local proxy between the real Claude Code and the API that applies policy to request and stream and forwards credential headers untouched.
A pure function called at each stream event boundary that returns pass, halt or alter, checked progressively against a budget.
The property that code in the route copies credential headers without reading, logging or storing them; checked by a canary scan.

name: claude route R1
claim: Messages stream events (text, thinking, tool_use, usage, stop reason) map to the harness OpenAI-style chunks with no loss for a text-only turn. (docs/platform/claude-route-survey.md R1)

name: claude route R2
claim: With the gateway harness listener speaking OpenAI-style SSE, the existing openaiCompatible provider plus opt.base serves the route with only a registry entry, needsKey false and a settings label. (docs/platform/claude-route-survey.md R2)

name: claude route R3
claim: No byte of a credential (a canary in the container env or in a fake auth header) appears in gateway logs, traces, stores, the page, the harness trace or an exported session, in either auth mode. (docs/platform/claude-route-survey.md R3)

name: claude route R4
claim: A halt ends the stream within one further event, delivers partial blocks, and the consumer (page or Claude Code) proceeds with its next request without error. (docs/platform/claude-route-survey.md R4)

name: claude route R5
claim: A per-delta counter halts within one delta of the budget and the token estimate stays within 25 percent of final usage output tokens over recorded turns. (docs/platform/claude-route-survey.md R5)

name: claude route R6
claim: Request-side thinking parameters lower thinking tokens per turn, and a harness-copy reducer over thinking text cuts kept thinking tokens without lowering task outcomes. (docs/platform/claude-route-survey.md R6)

name: claude route R7
claim: An alteration applies to the copy it is made on; Claude Code keeps what the model produced unless the alteration is made on the E stream itself. (docs/platform/claude-route-survey.md R7)

name: claude route R8
claim: A terse-style instruction plus a halt budget cuts output tokens per turn by a stated fraction without lowering completion, using a pure lexical check with a trace. (docs/platform/claude-route-survey.md R8)

name: claude route R9
claim: Later: with the harness transcript as source and the Claude Code session derived from it, a hash of the message list stays equal on both sides and cache reads stay high. (docs/platform/claude-route-survey.md R9)

name: claude route R10
claim: Later: with tool calls seen at the stream and one executor chosen per call, every tool call id runs exactly once, the host omitted where both targets could run it. (docs/platform/claude-route-survey.md R10)

name: claude route R11
claim: The gateway behaves the same with a user-supplied API key and with the users own signed-in binary, the mode chosen only by the container environment. (docs/platform/claude-route-survey.md R11)

name: claude route R12
claim: The page retries only before the first chunk, Claude Code retries stay its own and the gateway adds none, so a turn is never replayed or billed twice. (docs/platform/claude-route-survey.md R12)

name: claude route R13
claim: In pass-through mode the cache-hit ratio per turn over a 30-turn scripted session through the gateway is within 2 percentage points of the direct run. (docs/platform/claude-route-survey.md R13)

name: claude route R14
claim: The gateway adds under 5 ms per event at p95 and a halt ends the E stream with a synthetic stop sequence Claude Code accepts without retry or continue prompt. (docs/platform/claude-route-survey.md R14)

name: claude route R15
claim: cache_control normalisation does not lower the cache-hit ratio, raises it in at least one churn case, and keeps the system array order so the attribution block stays stripped. (docs/platform/claude-route-survey.md R15)

name: claude route R16
claim: The Claude Code listener forwards only requests with the Claude Code shape on the unpublished listener; the published listener never forwards a client-supplied credential upstream. (docs/platform/claude-route-survey.md R16)

name: claude route R17
claim: Dropping or editing a thinking block on the E stream causes a signature rejection and a Claude Code retry that costs the cache prefix, so E must not alter thinking. (docs/platform/claude-route-survey.md R17)

name: claude route R18
claim: Header values are copied without being read: a check using an access-throwing proxy object passes, and logs carry header names only. (docs/platform/claude-route-survey.md R18)
